messages:
anika (support): FYI customer acme-123 opened a ticket — p95/p99 shot up on /v1/generate around 09:20 UTC, getting timeouts and occasional 502s. They provided a few traces.
opsbot: Incident created: INC-2026-2134 (latency spike). Notifying #eng-sre and oncall.
mia (eng-sre): Can you paste the tenant id, model, region, and one trace id? any recent deploys?
anika (support): tenant=acme-123, model=redwood-13b-infer, region=us-west-2, trace=trace-0a3b, no deploys noted by customer since yesterday. Sample they've seen: p50 120ms, p95 600ms, p99 1.8s. They mentioned lots of tiny prompts (short SMS style).
sam (eng-runtime): I'm seeing a correlated change in batch hold windows for that tenant on us-west-2 since 09:18. avg_hold_ms increased from ~8ms -> ~110ms. Logs (excerpt):
```
[09:18:21] tenant=acme-123 route=continuous-batcher hold_ms=112 queue_len=3 prompt_bytes=48
[09:18:22] tenant=acme-123 route=continuous-batcher hold_ms=128 queue_len=2 prompt_bytes=34
[09:18:23] tenant=acme-123 route=continuous-batcher hold_ms=98  queue_len=1 prompt_bytes=22
```
jordan (eng-ml): Short prompts + low concurrency can push the batcher into waiting longer to fill batches (tradeoff: throughput vs latency). If prompt_bytes distribution skews small, the hold window will grow to try to reach max_batch_size which increases tail latency.
mia (eng-sre): Can we repro quickly with a local load test that mimics many tiny requests? Use this loop against staging:
```
for i in $(seq 1 500); do
  curl -s -X POST https://staging.redwood/api/v1/generate -H 'Authorization: Bearer $TEST' -d '{"input":"hi","max_tokens":16}' &
  sleep 0.01
done
wait
```
lee (oncall): I'm going to apply a tenant-level override to reduce hold_window_ms and enable the fast-path (unbatched small-reqs) as a hotpatch. Will roll to 5% canary first. commit: d4f7a8c.
opsbot: Deploy started: canary=5% override=acme-123 hold_window_ms=15 fastpath=true commit=d4f7a8c
(an update after ~2min)
anika (support): Customer reports immediate improvement on their end. p99 dropped to ~220ms, p95 ~90ms. They still see a couple of spikes but much better. :relieved:
sam (eng-runtime): Logs post-hotpatch show hold_ms now ~12-18ms for that tenant and batch sizes smaller, batcher routing hitting fast-path for ~65% of requests. Example logs:
```
[09:22:40] tenant=acme-123 route=fast-path processed_ms=14 prompt_bytes=28
[09:22:41] tenant=acme-123 route=continuous-batcher hold_ms=16 batch_size=4
```
jordan (eng-ml): Good quick mitigation. Longer-term we should add adaptive hold logic that adjusts target_hold based on observed prompt size quantiles and recent latency SLO violations. Also consider a tenant-level profile that defaults small-prompt tenants to fast-path.
mia (eng-sre): Filed ENG-8762 for adaptive hold window + tenant profiles. Action items: 1) keep override for acme-123 at canary until EOD, 2) monitor p99/p95 and error rates, 3) run reproducible load test and record results, 4) postmortem if we see regression again.
lee (oncall): Can confirm deploy rollback path ready (ops runbook step 4). If latency or errors reappear we'll rollback within 10m.
anika (support): I'll update the customer with the mitigation steps and ETA for a permanent fix. Thanks all. :thumbsup:
mia (eng-sre): Quick note — also saw a couple of 502s in the same window tied to a KV cache miss during batching handoff. Sam, can you link the small stacktrace to ENG-8763?
sam (eng-runtime): Yep, linking stacktrace and creating ENG-8763 for the KV handoff exceptions. Will include mitigation (retry/backoff) in the ticket.
opsbot: Incident INC-2026-2134 acknowledged by oncall lee. Status: mitigated (canary active).
